note: Ps86 David's personal prayer (17v). Passages: plea of the poor+godly v1-7; praise of the incomparable God v8-10; the request to be taught + united heart v11-13; deliverance from the insolent + closing plea v14-17. Human IB (rich): the POOR/NEEDY, GODLY self who TRUSTS; the CRYing + lifting of the SOUL; those who CALL; WORSHIP + GLORIFY; WALK in truth, the united HEART that FEARS; GIVE-THANKS with whole HEART; the INSOLENT/RUTHLESS who SEEK the life; the HATERS put to SHAME; being COMFORTED. God's incline/answer/gracious/merciful/steadfast-love/deliver = qualifiers; Sheol/depths/sign imagery = standalone.

dims.v: v1: 'answer me, for I am POOR (ani) and needy' - the lowly estate David pleads as his claim on God, humility the ground of the appeal.
v1: 'for I am poor and NEEDY (ebyon)' - the destitution that casts him wholly on God.
v2: 'PRESERVE my life (nephesh), for I am godly' - the self committed to God for keeping.
v2: 'preserve my life, for I am GODLY (chasid)' - the covenant-devotion David claims, not merit but belonging to God.
v2: 'save your servant who TRUSTS (batach) in you' - the reliance on God that undergirds every petition.
paired with the plea for grace
v3: 'for to you do I CRY (qara) all the day' - the ceaseless calling, prayer sustained through the whole day.
paired with lifting up the soul
v4: 'Gladden the SOUL (nephesh) of your servant' - the self longing for joy from God.
v4: 'for to you, O Lord, do I LIFT UP (nasa) my soul' - the aspiration of the whole self toward God, devotion as upward reach.
v4: 'do I lift up my SOUL (nephesh)' - the self raised toward God, the object of the aspiration.
v5: 'abounding in steadfast love to all who CALL (qara) upon you' - the invoking of God that his love answers.
paired with the plea for grace
v6: 'Give ear, O LORD, to my PRAYER (tephillah)' - the petition David lifts, asking to be heard.
v7: 'In the day of my trouble I CALL (qara) upon you' - the appeal in distress, confident of an answer.
v9: 'All the nations... shall come and WORSHIP (shachah) before you' - the homage of the peoples, worship as the destiny of the nations.
v9: 'and shall GLORIFY (kabad) your name' - the nations honouring God's name.
v11: 'that I may WALK (halak) in your truth' - the request to live in God's truth, obedience as the fruit of teaching.
paired with the fear of God's name
v11: 'UNITE my HEART (lebab) to fear your name' - the plea for an undivided heart, the inner self gathered to one devotion.
v11: 'unite my heart to FEAR (yare) your name' - the reverence that the united heart exists for, worship's single aim.
paired with the whole heart and glorifying
v12: 'I GIVE THANKS (yadah) to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart' - the gratitude of the whole self, thanksgiving vowed forever.
paired with the thanks and glorifying
v12: 'with my whole HEART (lebab)' - the entire inner self engaged in thanks, no reserve held back.
v12: 'and I will GLORIFY (kabad) your name forever' - the honouring of God vowed without end.
v13: 'you have delivered my SOUL (nephesh) from the depths of Sheol' - the self rescued from death, ground of the thanks.
v14: 'INSOLENT (zed) men have risen up against me' - the arrogant foes, pride turned to violence.
v14: 'a band of RUTHLESS MEN (arits) seeks my life' - the merciless enemies, violence without conscience.
paired with their disregard of God
v14: 'seeks my life, and they do not set you before them' - the murderous intent of the godless, malice that ignores God.
paired with being put to shame
v17: 'that those who HATE (sane) me may see and be put to shame' - the enemies' enmity, which God's help exposes.
by God's help to the psalmist
v17: 'may see and be PUT TO SHAME (bosh)' - the confounding of the foes when God vindicates his servant.
v17: 'because you, LORD, have helped me and COMFORTED (nacham) me' - the consolation God gives, the answered lament turned to comfort.
